name: Average ranks and significance
title: Average ranks and significance: comparing methods across datasets
blurb: The paper's headline comparison is a single average rank per method, computed over ten datasets. This section builds that number from zero: why raw scores from different datasets cannot be averaged, how a rank is computed and how tied scores are handled, and what the resulting number does and does not prove about a difference between two methods.
skip_hint: If you can compute an average rank from a table of per-dataset scores, apply the tied-ranks convention, and explain why a count of wins is not a significance test, skip this section.
